title: Infinitely many prescribed-frequency solutions of perturbed Schrodinger-Bopp-Podolsky systems in bounded domains: the critical-point Proposition 3.6
author: Danilo Gregorin Afonso, Bruno Mascaro
work: Existence of solutions with prescribed frequency for perturbed Schrodinger-Bopp-Podolsky systems in bounded domains
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026, No. 11, pp. 1--10; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.11; publisher version
difficulty_reason: The counted proposition states that the reduced functional of the perturbed Schrodinger-Bopp-Podolsky system has infinitely many critical points for every prescribed frequency, and it is the source-local step that yields the infinitely many prescribed-frequency solutions asserted by the main theorem of the article. Its complete proof must first record the evenness of the functional and the Palais-Smale property supplied by the source-local compactness lemma, and must then verify the two geometric hypotheses of the symmetric mountain pass theorem in two separate frequency regimes: below half of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue it has to produce a strict local minimum at the origin through a Poincare estimate with an epsilon absorption and the growth conditions on the perturbation, while above that threshold it has to split the space along the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian, choose the index at which the frequency crosses the spectrum and prove positivity of the functional on small spheres of the complementary subspace, using the sign of the frequency against that spectral splitting. This is a genuine research-level minimax verification for a fourth-order coupled system; it is graded H2 rather than H3 because the argument applies a named abstract critical point theorem with standard eigenvalue splitting rather than introducing a new compactness or deformation mechanism, the necessary compactness being supplied by the Palais-Smale lemma retained as complete context.
